diagnosis.summary: A traffic spike is active across all four services simultaneously. Request rates have risen 2.6x to 6.6x above baseline on product-service, cart-service, order-service, and payment-service. No 5xx errors have been recorded and order-service median latency remains in the low-millisecond range, indicating the stack is absorbing the load so far.
diagnosis.root_cause: A broad traffic surge across all services is the most likely root cause, with higher-than-proportional load reaching order-service and payment-service.
evidence: Request rates rose sharply on all four services: product-service from 14.98 to 38.52 rps (2.6x), cart-service from 2.05 to 8.13 rps (4.0x), order-service from 2.97 to 12.18 rps (4.1x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 6.25 rps (6.6x).
product-service DynamoDB read consumption rose from 449.3 to 1155.5 RCU/min (2.6x), tracking the increase in product-service request rate.
cart-service DynamoDB write consumption rose from 122.8 to 488.0 WCU/min (4.0x), in line with its request rate increase.

order-service DynamoDB write consumption rose from 56.6 to 375.0 WCU/min (6.6x) and read consumption rose from 60.8 to 178.5 RCU/min (2.9x), with writes growing disproportionately relative to the request rate increase.
order-service p50 latency rose from 3.6 ms to 14.1 ms (4.0x), remaining in the low-millisecond range.
product-service error_rate_5xx remains at 0, with no errors recorded despite the traffic increase.
recommended_actions: Monitor lambda_throttle_count on all four services to detect whether the shared Lambda concurrency limit is being approached under the elevated load.

Watch product-service db_consumed_read_capacity and read_throttle_events closely, as reads are already at 1155.5 RCU/min and further traffic growth could approach provisioned capacity; be prepared to raise provisioned read capacity or switch the Products table to on-demand.
Check whether the traffic surge is expected (a promotion, a launch, or a client retrying) before making any infrastructure changes, since latency and errors are currently within acceptable bounds.
If latency or error rates begin to climb, set rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to protect the stack while the source of traffic is investigated.
If lambda_throttle_count rises, request a higher account concurrency quota or use reserved concurrency to protect critical functions such as order-service and payment-service.
